claims.statement: The primary peer-reviewed phase 3 SYNCHRONIZE-1 results (76-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in n=725 adults with obesity without type 2 diabetes; published in the New England Journal of Medicine, PMID 42253238, doi 10.1056/nejmoa2600751) report, by the treatment-regimen estimand, mean body-weight change from baseline to week 76 of -12.2% with survodutide 3.6 mg and -13.0% with survodutide 6.0 mg, versus -5.4% with placebo (P<0.001 for both active doses vs placebo); 72.6% (3.6 mg), 71.9% (6.0 mg), and 46.3% (placebo) of participants achieved at least 5% weight loss. Independent professional-society coverage (Cleveland Clinic Journal of Medicine, ADA 2026) reports the same trial's efficacy estimand (the on-treatment effect among participants who remained on drug, excluding the impact of discontinuation/non-adherence) as 16.6% mean weight loss with the 6.0 mg dose -- the figure earlier reported by ConscienHealth. Both figures are legitimate, officially reported results from the same trial under two different, standard dual-estimand reporting conventions (the same convention used in other GLP-1/GCGR obesity trials, e.g. semaglutide, tirzepatide); the treatment-regimen estimand (-13.0%/-12.2%) is not more or less correct than the efficacy estimand (16.6%), and neither supersedes the other -- they answer different questions (effect of the assigned regimen as-treated-in-practice vs. effect while remaining on treatment).

context.population: adults with obesity or overweight with >=1 weight-related complication, without type 2 diabetes
context.formulation: survodutide 3.6 mg or 6.0 mg once weekly vs placebo
context.doseText: survodutide 3.6 mg or 6.0 mg once weekly with up-titration, 76-week trial protocol (SYNCHRONIZE-1); not a use recommendation

extractedEvidence.quote: At week 76, the mean change in body weight from baseline according to the treatment-regimen estimand was -12.2% (95% confidence interval [CI], -13.6 to -10.8) in the 3.6-mg group, -13.0% (95% CI, -14.4 to -11.6) in the 6.0-mg group, and -5.4% (95% CI, -6.9 to -4.0) in the placebo group; 72.6%, 71.9% and 46.3% of the participants, respectively, had weight reduction of at least 5% (P<0.001 for all comparisons with placebo).

The most common adverse events were gastrointestinal symptoms (typically mild to moderate), which occurred in 80.9% of the participants in the 3.6-mg group, in 89.7% of those in the 6.0-mg group, and in 47.9% of those in the placebo group. No deaths were reported.
